prompt: A platform has 24,000 Cassandra requests/s; one partition receives 4,800/s. Pending compaction is 1,200 GiB, processing is 100 MiB/s and new debt arrives at 70 MiB/s. Maximum replica outage is 20 h, repair scheduling delay 8 h, worst repair 26 h, margin 10 h and deletion grace 48 h. A vector collection has 15 million 768-dimension float32 points, two replicas and measured resident multiplier 1.7 per replica. ANN returns 17 of the exact top 20; p95 is 140 ms. A catalog backlog is 1.8 million entities, processes 800/s, receives 500/s and has a 90-minute freshness SLO. Produce a correctness-first capacity, containment, recovery, security, observability and cost plan with calculations.
directAnswer: Hold unsafe deletion-policy changes, unbounded compaction/repair, vector expansion and freshness-dependent catalog decisions. Cassandra hottest-key share is 4,800/24,000 = 20 percent, concentrated on one replica set; adding arbitrary nodes does not split it. Compaction net drain is 100-70 = 30 MiB/s, so 1,200 x 1,024 / 30 = 40,960 seconds or about 11.38 hours before overhead; preserve free space for rewrite, growth, repair/stream and reserve, and reduce admission if time-to-exhaustion is shorter. Repair safety requires 20+8+26+10 = 64 hours, which exceeds 48-hour grace by 16 hours, so current assumptions are unsafe; do not shorten grace and restore per-range repair/outage discipline or extend reviewed horizon. Raw vector bytes are 15,000,000 x 768 x 4 = 46,080,000,000 bytes, about 42.92 GiB. Estimated resident demand is 42.92 x 1.7 x 2 = about 145.9 GiB, before rebuild overlap and other unmeasured peaks. Recall@20 is 17/20 = 0.85; 140 ms is acceptable only if a declared per-slice quality gate allows 0.85, otherwise latency is irrelevant. Catalog net drain is 800-500 = 300 entities/s; drain time is 1,800,000/300 = 6,000 seconds = 100 minutes, already beyond the 90-minute SLO before stage overhead. Reduce arrivals or raise measured processing sufficiently, show as-of time and protect consumers. Use tenant-aware least privilege, encrypted/authenticated service paths, protected backups/snapshots/metadata, separate operator identities and audit. Validate Cassandra per-key/replica/repair/deletion and restore, vector identity/recall/memory/restore, and catalog source-to-index watermark/coverage/access. Track cost per correct operation, query meeting recall/latency and entity inside freshness—not raw throughput.
foundation: The tightest identity-specific correctness and capacity boundary governs the system. Average capacity, low latency and green jobs cannot substitute for deletion safety, retrieval quality or observation freshness.
reasoningSteps: Freeze unsafe mutations and preserve cross-service identity/time evidence.
Calculate 30 MiB/s net compaction and 11.38-hour ideal drain.
Calculate 64-hour repair requirement versus 48-hour grace gap.
Calculate 42.92 GiB raw and about 145.9 GiB replicated measured resident demand.
Calculate recall@20 of 0.85 and compare to sliced gate.
Calculate catalog 300/s net drain and 100-minute drain versus SLO.
Design admission, headroom, recovery and freshness containment.
Apply least privilege, encryption, audit and sensitive-copy lifecycle.
Validate user outcomes and outcome-linked unit cost.
seniorAnswer: I hold mutations first. The hot partition is 20 percent of all Cassandra traffic and remains on one replica set. Compaction ideally drains in 11.38 hours at net 30 MiB/s, but deletion safety is already invalid because the 64-hour outage/repair envelope exceeds 48-hour grace. Vector raw bytes are 42.92 GiB and the measured two-replica estimate is 145.9 GiB before rebuild headroom; recall@20 is only 0.85 despite 140-ms p95. Catalog drain is 100 minutes, beyond its 90-minute SLO. I contain each violated contract, restore verified versions/state, and admit work only against per-identity correctness plus measured capacity.
weakAnswer: Add nodes, run compaction faster, keep vector search because 140 ms is good, and wait for the catalog queue to clear.
whyWeak: It ignores the unsplit hot partition, deletion horizon violation, space and maintenance risk, retrieval quality, and a backlog whose ideal drain already breaches freshness.

followUps.prompt: What processing rate meets 90 minutes if arrivals remain 500/s?
followUps.answer: Required net drain is 1,800,000/5,400 = 333.33 entities/s, so total sustained processing must exceed 833.33/s; add margin and stage overhead, so 834/s is merely mathematical minimum, not an operating target.

followUps.prompt: What if vector points double during migration?
followUps.answer: Raw bytes and resident estimate approximately double for the new corpus, while coexistence with the old version and rebuild creates additional peak; measure and admit the full overlap before starting.

followUps.prompt: Can raising deletion grace alone fix repair?
followUps.answer: It can widen the evidence-retention horizon but also increases tombstone burden and does not fix skipped repair. Review storage/read impact and prove per-range completion.
